articleTitle: Mining Haulage Road Maintenance Prediction Dashboard Utilising Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper details the development of a predictive maintenance dashboard designed for haulage roads in surface mining operations using machine learning algorithms. We assessed various machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), to determine their effectiveness in predicting the timing and location of necessary road maintenance. The research identifies the Logistic Regression model as the most effective, which was trained on data including vibration measurements, equipment counts, and speed metrics to evaluate road surface conditions. These inputs are processed through a logistic function to estimate the probability of required repairs. The predictions generated by the model are stored in an SQL database and visualized through Power BI, which offers a user-friendly interface. This interface enables operators, including those with limited experience, to interpret the data effectively and make informed maintenance decisions, thus improving operational efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Recognition System for Hand-Drawn Sketches by Children with Down Syndrome
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Children with Down Syndrome (DS) often face challenges in traditional learning environments due to difficulties in encoding information and expressing their thoughts through conventional means. To address these challenges, this research presents the development and evaluation of a deep learning-based recognition system specifically designed for interpreting hand-drawn sketches by children with DS. The system aims to facilitate more effective communication and learning by accurately recognizing and analyzing these sketches, providing valuable insights into the cognitive and creative capabilities of the children. The proposed system utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify and interpret sketches drawn by DS children, comparing them with standard reference samples provided by educators. Our study focuses on the application of this system within an E-Learning environment, where it serves as a tool to enhance the educational experience by offering tailored feedback and support to each child based on their unique inputs. The system was tested on a dataset of hand-drawn images collected from local DS children, and the results demonstrated high accuracy in recognition and classification. Additionally, the system's performance was evaluated against traditional methods, showing significant improvements in both accuracy and the ability to adapt to the diverse drawing styles of the children. This research underscores the potential of deep learning technologies in creating more inclusive and effective educational tools for children with special needs, paving the way for further innovations in this field.

articleTitle: Enhancing G.C.E. Ordinary Level Mathematics Through Adaptive Learning in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Proficiency in mathematics is essential for both academic and professional success, yet many students find the subject difficult, especially when preparing for important exams like Sri Lanka's General Certificate of Education (G.C.E.) Ordinary Level examination. In Sri Lanka, the students show poor pass rates in Ordinary Level mathematics examination. In order to improve mathematics education for O/L students, this research suggests an innovative mobile application that makes use of adaptive learning strategies. This application features components like a comprehensive knowledge bank that is curriculum-mapped, pre-assessment tools for identifying knowledge shortages, a weaknesses based lesson recommendation for personalized lesson suggestions, a custom developed chat assistant to interact with the knowledge bank, interactive 3D visualizations and justifications of complex concepts, and platforms for problem-solving, writing, and time management skill development. The suggested adaptive learning strategy makes use of multimedia tools and datadriven insights to tailor instruction to each student's unique needs, improving math comprehension and readiness for the O/L examination in Sri Lanka.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Beehive Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been an alarming decline in bee populations both globally and in Sri Lanka, severely impacting ecosystems and agriculture worldwide. Traditional methods in Sri Lankan beekeeping are often time-consuming and less efficient, making hive management and health assessment challenging. This paper introduces a smart IoT-based beehive monitoring system tailored to the Sri Lankan beekeeping industry. The system integrates various sensors to measure key hive parameters, such as temperature, humidity, and weight, offering beekeepers a user-friendly web interface for real-time monitoring of hive conditions. It also provides insights into hive management aspects, including feeding needs, optimal harvesting times, and abnormal temperature detection within the hive. This paper highlights the initial steps towards implementing a robust IoT-based beehive monitoring system, acknowledging its current limitations. By addressing these limitations in the future, the authors aim to develop a more effective and efficient monitoring method for Sri Lankan beekeepers, saving time and enhancing the productivity and health of bee colonies.

articleTitle: Optimized Multi-Processor System-on-Chip (MPSoC) Design for Low-Resource JPEG Encoding
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of a Multiprocessor System-on-Chip (MPSoC) architecture for low-resource JPEG encoding. The initial design employs six Central Processing Units (CPUs) to implement a pipelined JPEG encoder, divided into stages: color space conversion, level shifting, discrete cosine transform (DCT), quantization, Huffman encoding, and output buffering. The pipeline is then optimized using custom hardware components, including First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queues, custom instruction blocks, and superscalar pipelines to improve performance and efficiency. The paper details the design process, various optimization strategies, implementation challenges, and the resulting performance improvements. The system is implemented and evaluated using the Cyclone IV E Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform with Nios II/e processors, and the design was developed using the Quartus II software, demonstrating significant gains in throughput and resource efficiency.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Browser Fingerprinting Based Approach for Web Bot Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Web bots are becoming increasingly sophisticated, posing a serious threat to internet security and integrity. In response to this growing issue, this study proposes a novel bot detection method based on browser fingerprinting and machine learning. The proposed method is a model that was trained on browser fingerprints collected from web traffic using a custom script with a browser fingerprinting library. The traffic was classified as legitimate or malicious based on firewall rules and honeypots. This model seeks to enhance bot detection accuracy while decreasing false positives, filling a gap in the existing research on browser fingerprint-based bot detection. The experimental results demonstrate that detailed browser fingerprint data can serve as an effective indicator for distinguishing between human and automated traffic, providing a foundation for integrating browser fingerprinting into wider security measures. The study also analyzes the specific attributes on browser fingerprints that contribute most significantly to differentiating between legitimate and bot traffic, while acknowledging the limitations in the proposed method.

articleTitle: Assessing Quality of Service Performance in SDN Controllers: POX vs. OpenDaylight
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This research offers a comparative analysis of Qual-ity of Service (QoS) within Software Defined Networks (SDN) by assessing the POX and OpenDaylight controllers across various network topologies. The results show that OpenDaylight has a 32.59% higher average throughput than POX, demonstrating its superior data handling capabilities. Conversely, POX exhibits a 54.53% lower average delay and an 85.05% higher average jitter compared to OpenDaylight, highlighting its effectiveness in maintaining lower latency and variability in packet transmission times. These contrasting performances provide essential insights for network engineers in selecting the optimal SDN controller based on specific network demands, significantly influencing the overall network efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: Galaxy Morphology Classification Based on VGG19 Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Galaxy morphology classification is crucial for understanding galaxy formation and evolution. Traditional methods for classifying galaxy morphologies are labour-intensive and require expert knowledge. Recent deep learning approaches simplify this process but often focus only on basic galaxy types, such as spiral, elliptical, and irregular, overlooking more complex or mixed morphologies. This study applied a transfer learning-based model for 10-class galaxy morphology classification using the Galaxy10 DECaLS dataset, which contains 17,736 images across 10 distinct galaxy types that diverge from the primary galaxy morphology types. The proposed classification model employed VGG19 as the base for feature extraction, supplemented by custom fully connected layers for classification. The approach included comprehensive data preprocessing, extensive data augmentation, the use of learning rate reduction and model checkpointing during training. A thorough evaluation using multiple metrics demonstrated significant improvements in classification performance, achieving 97.97% accuracy, 89.84% precision, 89.69% recall, an F1-score of 89.68%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98 on test data using macro-averaging. These findings confirmed the efficacy of deep learning models for automating galaxy morphology classification and underscored the benefits of transfer learning in achieving high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Context-Aware Input/Output Validation in Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The vulnerability of mobile applications to security risks due to inadequate input/output validation has been high-lighted. Conventional rule-based methods have found it difficult to adjust to changing attack surfaces and various environments. A unique method for context-aware input/output validation in mobile applications has been suggested, utilizing machine learning. The creation of a machine learning model that can instantly detect abnormal patterns by examining past data, app context, and user input sequences has been investigated. An adaptive validation system has been implemented based on the model's output, dynamically modifying the validation criteria. The efficacy and user experience of the system has been assessed through penetration testing and user research. It is anticipated that the findings will aid in the creation of mobile applications that are both safer and easier to use.

articleTitle: Advanced Convolutional Neural Networks for Detecting and Quantifying Infections in Coconut Tree Tissue Cultures
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Coconut tree cultivation is crucial for many tropical cultures, serving as a vital source of nutrition, income, and environmental stability. However, the traditional methods used in coconut tree tissue culture are not without challenges. Issues such as bacterial and fungal infections can significantly hamper the growth and productivity of coconut trees, limiting the effectiveness of tissue culture practices. These infections often go undetected in their early stages, making it difficult for farmers to take timely and effective action. This research proposes a novel approach to improving coconut tree tissue culture by integrating machine learning with agronomical expertise. Through advanced image analysis, the study enhances the identification and severity prediction of bacterial and fungal infections in tissue cultures. These insights lead to actionable recommendations for healthier trees and more efficient cultivation. Integrating technology with traditional expertise marks a significant advancement in addressing challenges faced by coconut farmers, offering a pathway to increased productivity, sustainability, and improved infection management, benefiting both farmers and the broader agricultural community.

articleTitle: Real World Data-Driven Agent-Based Modeling for Health Policy Insights During Epidemics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Pandemics and epidemics pose significant threats due to their rapid global spread, overwhelming healthcare systems, and causing high mortality and morbidity rates. The recent COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the urgent need for advanced tools to predict and manage infectious disease transmission in complex populations. While Agent-Based Models (ABMs) have become crucial in this context, many existing models oversimplify simulation environments and often fail to consider disease transmission through public transportation. In this study, we propose a framework that integrates a realistic environment and transportation model into the ABM, enhancing its accuracy in simulating airborne disease spread. Our framework is designed to be adaptable and generalizable, making it suitable for modeling various diseases. As a case study, we simulate COVID-19 transmission in the Kandy District, demonstrating how incorporating a realistic environment and transportation network improves the model's ability to reflect real-world conditions. This approach provides a more precise tool for disease propagation simulations within ABMs, offering valuable insights for public health strategies.

articleTitle: Dynamic Queue Management System for Multi-Cashier Supermarkets Using IoT and Real-Time Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Optimizing consumer satisfaction and operational efficiency in supermarkets hinges on effective queue management at cashier counters. In multi-cashier systems, customers often choose lines based on the number of people waiting, ignoring the number of items in each cart. This behavior leads to inefficient queue distribution, resulting in longer waits at counters with higher item counts and underutilized counters with fewer items, detracting from the shopping experience. This study proposes a dynamic queue management system leveraging Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras and Internet of Things (IoT) devices for real-time monitoring to enhance checkout efficiency. Our approach uses a robust object detection model, developed with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, to accurately determine queue lengths and cart contents from CCTV footage, identifying and categorizing customers and cashiers. IoT sensors count the items in each customer's cart, and this data is combined with CCTV footage to calculate the optimal cashier allocation. This system dynamically assigns customers to cashier counters based on the number of customers and the complexity of their transactions, distributing the checkout load more evenly and efficiently. Processed images, including visual annotations of queue lengths and optimal cashier assignments, are uploaded to Firebase for real-time viewing and access. This technology streamlines the checkout process, enhancing customer satisfaction and optimizing queue management by reducing wait times. The results demonstrate that dynamic queue assignment and real-time item counting significantly improve operational efficiency and customer happiness. This study provides valuable insights and advances in retail queue management, offering a more efficient and customer-focused approach to supermarket operations.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Large Language Models on Problem-Solving Skills of Undergraduates - A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-3 and GPT-4 in educational environments is rapidly transforming how undergraduate students approach problem solving tasks. This systematic literature review (SLR) aims to investigate the 32 studies that were published between 2021 and 2024 in order to assess the impact of LLMs on problem solving skills. The review identifies the significant improvements in undergraduates' problem-solving effectiveness, creativity, and computational thinking. It also emphasizes the need for careful implementation of these tools to avoid potential overreliance, which may impact the student's ability to develop independent problem-solving skills. The review identifies the importance of a well-balanced integration of LLMs in education to maximize their benefits while addressing the challenges they present. Recommendations for future research directions are suggested to further explore the long-term impacts of LLMs on the development of problem-solving skills and their applicability across diverse academic environments.

articleTitle: CARA: A Hybrid Framework Integrating Swarm AI Agents and Knowledge Graphs for Advanced LLM Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Language models excel in linguistic processing but often face challenges with complex reasoning tasks that require real-world interaction and multi-step logic. This paper presents the Cognitive Adaptive Reasoning Architecture (CARA), a framework that enhances reasoning by integrating a modular swarm architecture with knowledge graphs (KGs) and specialized agents. These agents, equipped with diverse tools, dynamically adapt to various tasks, actively engaging with real-world data. CARA's continuous memory update cycle ensures each reasoning step is based on up-to-date, contextual KG knowledge, enhancing decision-making. Incorporating human insights further aligns outcomes with nuanced cognition. Experimental results demonstrate CARA's superior performance over larger models, advancing language models' reasoning capabilities for more context-aware, informed decision-making in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Smart Water Management System for Rainwater Harvesting Tanks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Rainwater Harvesting Tanks (RWHTs) have been built in many rural areas of Sri Lanka due to the challenges in water scarcity and water quality. However, these tanks lack effective monitoring and management, resulting in inefficient water usage and health risks from potential contamination. Households face challenges managing water during fluctuating rainfall, with no guidance on diverting water or communication with distributors and neighbors for water access when supplies are low. The proposed solution monitors real-time availability, pH and turbidity levels of water by the usage of data collected from loT sensors. Water consumption of the household is dynamically predicted in order to compare with the current availability to show for how long the water will last. The solution uses Facebook Prophet and Random Forest for dynamic predictions, You Only Look Once Version 8 (YOLOv8) for debris detection alerts, and Linear Regression to forecast rainfall, helping households manage water effectively. The water requests received to the purified water distributor are prioritized using the Timsort algorithm to efficiently deliver the water to the customers. The proposed solution also introduces a network of connected tanks for efficient water transfer between households. The entire system was implemented in a selected rainwater harvesting tank in Parasangaswewa village in Sri Lanka. The entire system was tested to identify whether all the functionalities behave as expected. This resulted in ensuring the implementation of the smart water management system operates reliably, efficiently, and meets the needs of households for sustainable water usage and distribution.

articleTitle: Sagittarius: Floating Self Navigating Robot for Monitor the Water Quality of Rural Reservoirs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal solution for monitoring water quality in Sri Lanka, where reservoirs are essential for daily life and agriculture, especially in rural areas. Despite its importance, 3.6 million communities are affected by severe water quality problems, contributing to a high incidence of chronic kidney diseases. While water purification plants are the only solution, high salinity and hardness often make these sources unsuitable. Many rural reservoirs remain unpurified but could potentially provide safe water if properly monitored and maintained. Yet water sources are frequently contaminated by chemical waste and activities associated with agricultural business but effective solutions for continuous water quality monitoring are lacking. This study introduces an autonomous robot equipped with advanced sensors to monitor critical water quality parameters in real-time. By integrating machine learning for data analysis and prediction, Sagittarius enables continuous assessment of reservoir water quality, providing timely insights for public health protection. Field tests demonstrate a prediction accuracy exceeding 98.5%, supporting proactive water management and monitoring. This system has shown potential to aid in early detection of contamination, informing authorities promptly for preventive actions, and enabling sustainable water usage. This solution can significantly contribute to public health protection and informed water resource management decisions.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Interaction System for Speech-Based Autism Intervention in Sinhala-Speaking Sri Lankan Children using the NAO Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper presents a multimodal interaction system designed for speech-based autism intervention in Sinhala-speaking Sri Lankan children, utilizing the NAO robot. The system integrates four components, language content detection, dialog management, voice synthesis, and gesture synthesis, to create an engaging and adaptive therapeutic environment. By leveraging these technologies, the system provides real-time, personalized responses that align with the cultural and linguistic needs of Sinhala-speaking children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The NAO robot facilitates natural and supportive interaction through synchronized speech and gestures, aiming to improve communication and social skills in children with ASD. Preliminary evaluations demonstrate the potential of the system to enhance engagement and responsiveness in therapy sessions, marking a significant step forward in developing specialized interventions for autism in non-Western, non-English-speaking contexts.

articleTitle: A Fully Featured and Optimized Object Document Mapper for the Go Programming Language
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The Go programming language has seen a rise in popularity because of its straightforward nature and efficient performance. However, it still lacks a dependable and fully featured Object Document Mapper (ODM) for working with document databases like MongoDB. Many existing ODMs either miss critical features or have fallen out of active development, which can lead to messy code and added complexity. To address these issues, this study presents “Elemental,” a robust and optimized ODM built specifically for Go. Elemental is equipped with a powerful query builder, seamless middleware integration, and advanced data aggregation tools that work across multiple database connections. Test results have shown that Elemental outperforms the official MongoDB driver in both performance and maintainability, making it a suitable choice for Go enterprise applications. The obtained benchmarks and metrics indicate that the Elemental ODM provides shorter execution times, reduces cyclomatic complexity, and has a higher maintainability index. This study concludes that Elemental ODM significantly improves the developer experience and efficiency of software development by providing a well refined set of tools.

articleTitle: Optimizing User Experience Through Machine Learning: A Review of Key Tools and Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The application of machine learning (ML) to user experience (UX) design is the subject of this study, with a particular focus on privacy concerns, bias mitigation, and the development of best practices for ethical ML implementation. It evaluates several ML tools, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Azure, BigQuery, alongside design platforms like Figma, can be assessed for their effectiveness in optimizing UX workflows, enhancing user satisfaction, and improving system adaptability. A comprehensive literature review identifies gaps in the current research, such as the need for more robust, user-centered frameworks and a lack of detailed analysis regarding the long-term impacts of ML-driven UX systems. The study emphasizes the critical importance of collaboration between ML experts and UX designers to create more efficient, inclusive, and user-friendly systems while maintaining high ethical standards in data use. Furthermore, it explores emerging technologies, such as augmented and virtual reality, that are expected to influence the future of ML-UX integration. These findings offer valuable guidance for both practitioners and researchers aiming to leverage ML's potential in UX design. Ultimately, this review contributes to the broader discourse by providing recommendations that address innovation, ethical challenges, and responsible implementation across diverse digital design contexts.

articleTitle: “AI-Driven SMART K9 CARE SYSTEM” – A Comprehensive System for Reducing Canine Anxiety During Owner Absence
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The Smart K9 Care System is an innovative solution designed to support the emotional, physical, and behavioral needs of dogs, especially when their owners are away. Combining advanced technologies like IoT devices, machine learning, and real-time data monitoring, the system offers a holistic approach to canine care. It includes a heart rate monitor, activity tracker, smart treat dispenser, and a safety mechanism that tracks the dog's location. These components detect anxiety by analyzing data from a smart belt with sensors monitoring heart rate, movement, and other vital signs. The heart rate and activity trackers provide continuous insights into the dog's physiological and movement patterns. The smart treat dispenser comforts anxious dogs with personalized feeding schedules, calming scents, and playback of the owner's voice, while the safety mechanism secures the environment, preventing escapes and accidental ingestion of harmful substances. This data is processed through machine learning models to predict anxiety levels, enabling timely interventions via a mobile app. Tested in various conditions, the system has proven reliable and adaptable, enhancing the quality of life for dogs and supporting owners in managing their pets' well-being.

articleTitle: A BERT-Based Approach to Keyword Search for Digital Evidence Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Existing forensic tools, especially those relying on traditional keyword searches, often fall short in efficiency and accuracy. These tools are vulnerable to human error, bias, and investigator fatigue, which can result in the omission of crucial evidence, thereby undermining the success of investigations. Keyword searching, although a widely used technique across various types of digital investigations, frequently proves inadequate when faced with complexities such as large data volumes, data variety, unstructured data, and context-dependent information of modern data sets. This research presents an innovative AI-powered approach to keyword searching designed to overcome the complexities of traditional methods. By incorporating advanced Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), a machine learning (ML) algorithm, and natural language processing (NLP) techniques, the proposed identifies relevant terms and entities within large and complex data sets. This approach accelerates the investigative process and has a final accuracy of approximately 92.5%, reducing the risk of overlooking critical evidence by leveraging techniques like semantic search, contextual understanding, and conceptual matching to identify relevant information even when exact keywords or variations are not used. The adoption of AI-driven keyword searching is expected to transform digital forensic investigations by providing a more reliable, efficient, and comprehensive tool for evidence discovery.

articleTitle: Towards an Ontological Digital Forensic Investigation Framework for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The growing presence of autonomous vehicles (AVs) on our roads has been applauded by many people, including those in the transportation, military, and logistics industries. However, an equally growing concern about AVs is that they raise new cybersecurity challenges, including the need for a robust digital forensic investigation framework to investigate incidents or criminal activities involving AVs. Of more concern is that traditional digital forensic methods have been found wanting when investigating incidents involving AVs. This is primarily due to the complex interplay of sensors, software, and human interaction involved in AV operation. In this research, therefore, the authors review existing digital forensic investigation frameworks for AVs and then analyse their strengths, weaknesses, and suitability for addressing various AV forensic challenges. Additionally, we analyse the potential legal and ethical implications of digital forensic investigations in AV contexts. The authors aim to identify key AV forensic challenges and future directions through this research. As a new contribution, the authors propose high-level ontological digital forensic investigation framework components as a starting point towards a comprehensive framework and the basis for further exploration and future research. This includes the future implementation of the proposed components into a fully-fledged ontological framework that supports efficient and reliable digital forensic investigation processes for autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Rear-End Collision Avoidance Using Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This research paper offers a novel approach to detect rear-end collisions and increase the acceleration of the victim car to possibly avoid or minimize the impact of the collision. A Deep Q-Learning model is utilized to predict the collision, the optimum acceleration of the victim car and the optimum braking of the committer car. The study uses a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in a simulated environment, focusing on synchronized responses between lead and following vehicles. A comprehensive reward function encourages safe driving behaviors, optimized braking, and successful obstacle detection and avoidance. The continuous action space allows for subtle vehicle control, enhancing the system's adaptability to various collision scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate an overall improvement in collision avoidance and impact reduction over 5000 training episodes. This approach addresses a critical gap in existing safety systems by specifically targeting rear-end collisions, offering the potential for a significant reduction in accident rates and severity. Future work includes real-world testing and expansion to more complex traffic scenarios.

articleTitle: Understanding Catchment Impacts: Enhanced Water Level Prediction with LSTM and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Flooding is a significant global challenge, impacting millions annually and causing extensive damage to property and infrastructure. This growing threat is exacerbated by climate change and shifting monsoon patterns. Sri Lanka, with its complex geography of central mountains and extensive river basins, faces increasing flood risks due to these climatic changes. To address these pressing issues, the study introduces an LSTM-based approach integrated with explainable AI to enhance flood prediction capabilities. The methodology involves a systematic approach to data collection and structuring, including a context-based pre-processing method tailored to Sri Lanka's specific geographical characteristics. The research presents a comprehensive modeling approach for predicting water levels and incorporates explainable AI techniques to assess the impact of each catchment area on prediction outcomes, aiming to provide greater transparency in the prediction process and a clearer understanding of the model's decision-making. The model achieved a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.000431 and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0208, indicating relatively low prediction errors and suggesting that the predictions closely approximate the observed water levels. The study effectively assessed the impact of each catchment area and identified the Rathnapura catchment as the primary contributor to flooding in the targeted region of the Kalu Ganga River. This research is crucial for improving flood management strategies and mitigating the risks associated with flooding in vulnerable regions.

articleTitle: Multi-Model System for Sustainable Coral Reef Conservation in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Coral reefs, often called the “rainforests of the sea”, are vital ecosystems supporting 25% of all marine species and providing significant ecological, economic, and coastal protection benefits. However, they are under severe threat from climate change, pollution, and overfishing, leading to widespread degradation. This research presents an automated framework designed to enhance the efficiency of ongoing coral conservation efforts. The proposed methodology integrates advanced technologies, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with cross-domain transfer learning for accurate species identification and growth monitoring. A hybrid scheduling algorithm, incorporating AHP, TOPSIS, and Reinforcement Learning (RL), optimizes task prioritization. Resource and labor allocation is refined using Explainable AI (XAI), while a Knowledge Graph Convolutional Network (KGCN) enhances real-time recommendations. This approach achieves 94.2% accuracy in species identification, 85% accuracy in growth monitoring, optimizes task prioritization with a 95% task completion rate and 90% resource utilization efficiency, while real-time recommendations achieve an AUC of 0.964 and an F1 score of 0.921. These results significantly improve the precision, adaptability, and efficiency of coral restoration activities, ensuring more sustainable and responsive conservation strategies.

articleTitle: An Integrated Framework for Demographic Analysis, Person Recognition, and Path Tracking in Surveillance Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Public safety brings up a critical need for smart surveillance systems that go beyond the methodology conventions by providing a more in-depth, data-driven approach. This study proposes an important framework for person identification, demographic prediction, and path tracking to enhance situational awareness in monitored areas. Face recognition and gait analysis using MobileNet and VGG16 models have reached up to 94.8% and 98.5%, respectively, while predictions of age and gender are performed to provide demographic insights. The combination of YOLOv5 and Kalman filtering improved the path tracking accuracy from 64.68% to 88.45%, dealing with ID consistency and smoothing trajectories during occlusions, with an IoU of 0.86. The visual insights are enriched further using heatmaps to show high-activity zones and popular routes. Contextual path annotation with directional arrows and color-coded paths affords intuitive summarization that allows actionable insight into movement patterns and congregation areas. This will be a considerable stride forward toward a data-driven approach in surveillance for public safety.

articleTitle: Estimating Story Points in Scrum: Balancing Accuracy and Interpretability with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Accurate story point estimation is crucial for agile software development. Manual estimation is time-consuming and error-prone, leading to project delays and budget overruns. This study introduces a novel data preprocessing approach to address these challenges. Our method combines similar user story removal with conflicting story point values and data augmentation, distinguishing it from prior research. We contribute 3 new public datasets to support this research. Our experiments demonstrate the proposed preprocessing significantly enhances model accuracy, with the Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieving the highest performance (43.21%) compared to Bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) (42.37%). We use Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and Transformer-Interpret to enhance model interpretability. Among the explored interpretability approaches, highlighting relevant words proved the most effective for understanding model behavior. A human-centered evaluation assessed the model performance and reliability of the explainability methods. While both SVM and BERT had limitations in replicating human estimations, SVM performed marginally better. SHAP outperformed LIME and Transformer-Interpret in aligning with human reasoning, effectively capturing salient data aspects and showing promise for enhancing human-AI collaboration in agile development. Our findings contribute to advancing story point estimation accuracy and transparency in agile software development.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Framework for Exploring Customized CNN with Customer Demographics and Salon Visuals
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This research explores the integration of visual aesthetics and demographic data to enhance customer satisfaction in the beauty salon industry through a custom Convolutions Neural Network (CNN) model. Traditional salon experiences rely on visual elements such as interior design, ambiance, and branding, which shape customer perceptions. However, the influence of demographic factors such as age, gender, and income on these visual cues has been under explored. To address this gap, a CNN model was developed to combine visual and demographic inputs, enabling the prediction of customer preferences and segmentation. By analyzing images of salon environments and integrating customer data, the model offers actionable insights for salon owners to optimize design and services. The findings show that the custom CNN, enhanced with self-attention mechanisms, achieved high accuracy in predicting customer preferences, with a training accuracy of 98.1 % and a validation accuracy of 98.7%. This approach has practical applications in improving salon strategies and customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Integrating Deep Learning for Plant Growth Monitoring and Browning Disease Severity Identification in Coconut Tissue Culture
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The research aimed to address the inefficiencies and inaccuracies associated with manual plant growth measurement methods at the Coconut Research Institute (CRI). Deep learning algorithms were employed to automate the analysis of plant growth factors, including leaf size, leaf count, root length, and stem growth. Images of coconut tissue culture plants were collected and processed, followed by data augmentation to enhance model accuracy. The YOLOv8 model was utilized for the detection of flasks and the segmentation of leaves and stems. Through iterative training and augmentation, models with improved precision, recall, and Mean Average Precision (mAP) metrics were developed. The model, trained on an augmented dataset with 50 epochs, demonstrated significant improvements in segmentation tasks, achieving a precision of 0.925 and mAP50 of 0.884. For flask detection, a smaller dataset and pre-trained weights led to the selection of a model with a precision of 0.990 and mAP50 of 0.995. Root classification was performed using a YOLOv8 model, with the highest accuracy observed in the sharpened dataset (0.6977). Additionally, four CNN models were tested for browning disease classification, with InceptionV3 achieving the highest accuracy of 96%. The study demonstrates that deep learning models, particularly YOLOv8 and InceptionV3, are effective in automating plant growth monitoring and disease detection, significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of data collection at the Coconut Research Institute in Sri Lanka(CRISL). The results provide a foundation for the broader application of these models in the agricultural domain, enhancing overall plant health management.

articleTitle: GlowUp - Enhancing Salon Experience through AI-Driven Customer Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The GlowUp platform is an advanced solution that will reshape and refresh the salon industry by increasing customer satisfaction and improving efficiency in operations through the merging of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies. Its use of customized Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for analyzing salon design preferences, Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) for personalized hair and facial care recommendations, as well as Bidirectional Encoder Representations (BERT) for Natural Language Processing (NLP), which gives beautician recommendations based on customer reviews, this integrated system ensures personalized beauty solutions are delivered seamlessly, catering to specific customer needs and wants. The modern approach of GlowUp improves the customer experience, creating insights into how salons can improve their services. This high level of accuracy is backed by extensive validation through testing and user feedback, thus showing the potential to define new benchmarks in the field. Thus, this research reveals the significant advancements in AI and ML, demonstrating their application in revolutionizing personalized beauty care and salon management.

articleTitle: Efficient Path Estimation via Sensor Fusion of IMU, GPS, and Wheel Encoder and Control Parameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: In autonomous vehicles, precise estimation of control parameters is essential for ensuring safety, adaptability, and energy efficiency. However, standalone estimators often fall short due to their inability to detect sharp turns, wheel skidding, and slippage, along with their high computational demands. This study presents a fusion model that integrates GPS, IMU, and wheel encoder data to accurately estimate control parameters while maintaining safety and adaptability under varying environmental conditions. The model also determines the optimal tack of the vehicle using these estimated parameters. Extensive testing demonstrated the model's superior ability to detect subtle changes, identify wheel skidding and slippage, and outperform state-of-the-art stand alone and fusion models in computational efficiency. This research marks a significant advancement in au-tonomous vehicle technology, offering a robust and sophisticated tool for precise control parameter estimation and optimal path prediction.

articleTitle: Combating Digital Deception: Machine Learning Approaches for Detecting Political Misinformation and Clickbait on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper presents machine learning-based strategies for mitigating the problem of misinformation in social media, with a special focus on political misinformation detection and clickbait detection. The following research work attempts to address the pressing issue of the rapid spread of false or misleading information by making use of deep recurrent neural networks (RNN s) combined with semi-supervised learning methodologies. For political misinformation detection, a hybrid model integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with fully connected layers was developed, achieving 94.22 % accuracy on the CIC Truth Seeker dataset. Clickbait detection was made using a sequential architecture that combines LSTM and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) layers with Simple RNN layers to achieve an accuracy of 96% on test data. This study underlines the effectiveness of different machine learning techniques in battling misinformation that would contribute to online dignity in political discourse and ensure better public communication in a digital world.

articleTitle: SmartDine: A Comprehensive System for Enhancing Customer Satisfaction and Optimizing Business Operations in the Restaurant Context
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This research explores the integration of real-time video analysis, deep learning techniques, and advanced data processing tools to enhance customer satisfaction and operational efficiency in restaurant management. Leveraging CCTV footage, along with tools such as Python,PyTorch, OpenCV, and advanced models like YOLOv10 for object detection and YOLO-pose for key point extraction, the study focuses on optimizing key aspects such as food satisfaction analysis, customer engagement and wait time reduction, optimal use and planning of resources. Custom models, including an LSTM network, analyze detected key points to identify customer actions and estimate time spent on various activities. Data augmentation techniques enhance model performance, with metrics like precision and recall used for evaluation. The study further aims to provide restaurant managers with a dynamic dashboard that tracks real-time insights, including table turnover rates, preferred menu items, and optimal resource allocation. This research contributes to data-driven restaurant management by offering a robust framework for real-time operational analysis, ultimately improving decision-making and enhancing the dining experience.

articleTitle: Telco Customer Churn Prediction Using Composite Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Customer churn is a critical issue in the telecommunication (Telecom) industry, leading to significant revenue loss and increased customer acquisition costs. To address this, a project was initiated to reduce home broadband (HBB) postpaid churn from 20% within three months. This study introduces novel hybrid deep learning (DL) models, such as BiLSTM, CNN, and BiLSTM+CNN, which combine bidirectionallonglshortterm memory (BiLSTM) with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to enhance churn prediction accuracy. Additionally, the study explores the significance of feature selection in churn prediction and the potential of DL to automate this process, eliminating the need for expert intervention. Experimental results reveal that the BiLSTM model achieves a notable 76% precision when trained, tested, and validated on benchmark datasets, outperforming other DL techniques in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The study emphasizes the importance of data pre-processing and feature engineering, highlighting the significance of analyzing data usage patterns and household connections. Moreover, it suggests actionable strategies for Telecom companies to mitigate churn, such as targeted campaigns based on predicted churn reasons.

articleTitle: Detection of Fake Reviews in E-Commerce Platforms Related to Ayurvedic Cosmetics in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: The Ayurvedic cosmetics industry in Sri Lanka is grappling with the prevalence of fake reviews. To mitigate this problematic situation, this study first utilized Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze English-language un-structured text reviews from popular e-commerce platforms. Then, it incorporated three primary approaches: a rule-based algorithm, a machine learning model using logistic regression, and a deep learning model based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to identify fake news. Initially, rules for the rule-based al-gorithm were crafted with guidance from existing literature. This research investigated various feature engineering techniques and model architectures to enhance prediction accuracy and assessed the model performance through precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. The rule-based approach yielded a 50% accuracy, which was sub-optimal. However, the Logistic Regression model and the LSTM model obtained 89% and 80% accuracies respectively, out of which the LR model shows the highest accuracy. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of AI-based technologies in detecting fake reviews, thereby fostering a more transparent and ethical market for Ayurvedic cosmetics in Sri Lanka.

articleTitle: User-Centric Design of Contactless Smart Wheelchair System for Elderly People
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Using hand gesture recognition to improve mobility and independence, the study offers a user-centric design of a contactless wheelchair navigation system suited for senior citizens. The system utilizes the MediaPipe method to extract hand gesture data, allowing navigation based on five predefined gesture categories. By minimizing the necessity for physical contact and hence lowering strain and potential harm, this technique guaranteed users a smooth and intuitive control experience. The wheelchair's control system has been engineered to maneuver efficiently and avoid obstacles (using the SLAM + <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> * algorithm), improving user safety and dependability. The proposed navigation system proved helpful in real-world circumstances, with an overall accuracy of 90.23 ± 1.13 %. Furthermore, the hand gesture recognition model demonstrated strong performance in understanding user commands with an accuracy of 91.55 ± 1.55 %. For older adults who require wheelchair navigation that is safe, effective, and user-friendly, this novel approach presented a possible answer.

articleTitle: Predicting Employee Attrition & Employee Retention Period using Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper employs machine learning (ML) to predict employee retention and attrition during recruitment. Predictions assist decision-makers in selecting the most suitable long-term candidates while reducing the likelihood of losing current employees unexpectedly. The study used a mid-scale apparel company's corporate human resource dataset, which included pre- and post-recruitment information. The algorithms “SVM,” “Decision Tree,” and “Random Forest” were chosen for model construction based on the literature. Relevant metrics from six experiments using different inputs were presented. The Random Forest (RF) classifier outperformed the others in five of the six experiments. The RF algorithm outperformed both models, with an accuracy of 94.5% for retention and 89.7% for attrition prediction. Additional metrics, including Balanced Accuracy, Recall, Precision, and F1 Score, confirmed that RF is the most effective algorithm. A user interface predicted employee retention. A dashboard of active employees was created using the attrition prediction model. Demographic and job factors are distinguished to determine employee turnover causes. Gender was the most important demographic factor, while salary was the most important job factor.

articleTitle: Real-time Quality Monitoring System for the Apparel Industry in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper introduces SeamSense, an innovative real-time quality monitoring system aimed at transforming the apparel industry's quality control process in Sri Lanka. By automating the traditionally manual quality inspection, SeamSense targets the detection of seam defects using high-definition video capture, fog computing, and advanced machine learning models, particularly You Only Look Once 8 and You Only Look Once 9. These models are optimized for real-time seam defect identification, focusing on high-low and open-seam defects through advanced feature extraction and rapid processing. SeamSense is projected to reduce seam defects by approximately 30-40%, thus enhancing overall production quality. Beyond defect detection, SeamSense achieves optimized database management, strengthened security, and improved defect prediction accuracy. This is achieved through techniques such as motion-adaptive frame extraction, model-based augmentation, and fusion models. The fusion model uniquely integrates traditional machine learning with time-series analysis, enabling a comprehensive approach to quality control that supports consistent and high-standard apparel production. In doing so, SeamSense drives significant improvements in efficiency and innovation across the garment manufacturing sector.

articleTitle: Adaptive Continual Learning for Defect Detection in Dynamic Textile Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: In the textile industry, ensuring high product quality is challenging due to complex designs and the demand for customization. Traditional manual inspection is labor-intensive and inaccurate, making it unsuitable for modern production. This research proposes an advanced automated defect detection system that integrates a design specific auto-encoder and a common defect detection module. The auto-encoder learns and reconstructs textile patterns to detect subtle anomalies in new designs without requiring labeled or defective data. Concurrently, the common defect module recognizes common defects across various fabrics. The system uses active learning to optimize retraining and continual learning to adapt to new data without forgetting past knowledge. Experimental results show significant improvements in accuracy and robustness, reducing the need for frequent retraining and enhancing defect detection efficiency, thus supporting high quality textile production.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Science Education: A Systematic Review of Gamified Learning Platforms for Decision-Making Skills Development
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Data science is rapidly growing and impacting nearly every industry and research domain. As demand for skilled data scientists rises, data science education must prepare students not only with technical proficiency but also with the ability to make informed, data-driven decisions. Understanding the consequences of their decisions is crucial for data scientists. However, many data science students struggle to develop decision making skills due to insufficient practical experience and lack of exposure to real-world scenarios in their training. To address this gap, integrating realistic, interactive learning environments into educational platforms is essential. This paper presents a systematic literature review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, to explore notable features of learning environments that enhance practical learning in data science education. The review identifies a significant need for platforms that enable students to engage with scenarios replicating real world decision-making complexities. Evidence from fields like business, healthcare, and engineering shows that gamification can enhance decision-making skills, suggesting similar approaches could be effective in data science education. By analyzing existing literature, this paper demonstrates the potential of gamified platforms to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, better preparing future data scientists with technical skills and informed decision-making abilities.

articleTitle: A Generative Adversarial Network to Upscale the Resolution of Low-Resolution Galaxy Images
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: High-resolution galaxy images play a crucial role in astronomy and astrophysics, enabling detailed morphological analysis, the identification of faint structures, and distance measurements. However, limitations in telescope technologies, atmospheric conditions, and the vast distances of observed objects often result in low-resolution images. In this research, we leveraged advanced deep-learning methods to enhance the resolution of low-resolution galaxy images. We introduced a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) specifically developed to upscale galaxy images taken at suboptimal resolutions, with the Enhanced Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (ESRGAN) serving as the foundational model. Our self-attention multi-scale GAN architecture utilized deep learning to produce super-resolution images by learning from a dataset of high-resolution galaxy images. Additionally, we incorporated an Explainable AI technique to open the black box of our GAN model, providing insights into its intrinsic decision processes and feature learning mechanisms. This advanced approach not only enhanced image resolution but also improved model transparency and built trust in the model's predictions. Our results demonstrated a significant improvement in the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio and Structural Similarity Index Measure and provided a better understanding of the model's operations, which is highly important for scientific analysis and validation in astronomical research.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation of E-Learning Website
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: E-learning programs are designed to provide knowledge effectively, share information, and support learners in their educational endeavors. The success of these programs relies heavily on the usability of the e-learning applications, which must adhere to core usability principles. This study, in connection with the evaluation of the usability of the MOODLE e-learning platform, focuses specifically on users with various disabilities, the demographic that has been insufficiently addressed in prior research, aimed at the above facts. The research was conducted in two phases: the first involved reviewing literature and expert evaluations to establish and refine usability criteria. These criteria were then used in the second phase to develop a conceptual model for assessing usability based on effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction. Effectiveness and efficiency were evaluated by using the think-aloud protocol, while satisfaction was measured through a questionnaire. A total of 100 respondents participated in the study, and the collected data were analyzed by using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). This research not only fills a critical gap in existing usability studies but also aims to enhance the inclusivity and accessibility of the MOODLE platform for all users, ensuring that e-learning solutions are equitable and effective for a diverse range of learners.

articleTitle: Assistive Cartesian Healthcare Robot for Forearm Vein Puncturing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Venipuncture is essential for diagnosis and therapy, but it frequently has problems with vein identification and needle placement precision, which can result in consequences like bruises and bleeding. The proposed medical robot uses Cartesian coordinate mechanisms to locate and puncture forearm veins with low discomfort, producing precise and repeatable movements, especially under intelligent healthcare. The device combines cutting-edge sensor and image technology to pinpoint the best places for punctures and direct the placement of needles. By reducing human error, enhancing patient outcomes, and optimizing healthcare workers' workflow, this innovation seeks to make venipuncture operations more dependable and effective. The experiment findings indicate a promising breakthrough in healthcare robots for increased accuracy and cost-efficiency, with 90.9 % accuracy in box prediction, 94.9 % in vein segmentation, and 98.7 % in vein puncturing. The proposed mechanism can be used for automated tasks.

articleTitle: Crafting Tomorrow's Trends with Automated Precision, Efficiency, and Faultless Excellence in Apparel Industry for Medium Scale Businesses
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of Sri Lanka's apparel industry, the predominance of manual methods in the pre-production phase necessitates innovative technological interventions to enhance efficiency. This research explores the complexities of garment production, addressing critical challenges such as machine breakdowns, maintenance, and workforce management. By employing advanced technologies such as image recognition, loT devices, and machine learning, this study aims to transform pre-production decision-making, optimize sewing machine performance, implement predictive maintenance strategies, and refine workforce optimization. These initiatives, driven by domain expertise and cutting-edge methodologies, not only aim to bridge existing gaps in the industry but also pave the way for significant advancements, ensuring a future characterized by precision, efficiency, and operational excellence.

articleTitle: Assisting Hearing Impaired Children by Personalized Gamification of Auditory Verbal Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Children with hearing impairments often need to adapt to their hearing aids or cochlear implants through various techniques, with Auditory Verbal Therapy (AVT) being a prominent long-term method. AVT, led by auditory and speech clinical experts, involves four key stages: awareness, discrimination, identification, and comprehension, as outlined in the auditory skills checklist. To enhance the effectiveness of AVT and maintain the children's engagement, this study integrates personalized gamification into the therapy process. Focusing primarily on the comprehension stage, which aligns with daily human interactions, the study utilizes patient profiles and clinical suggestions to generate quiz-like activities. Prompt engineering and Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation were conducted to ensure gamification efficacy. To develop the most effective prompts to generate assistive activities for AVT, prompt engineering techniques were utilized. Additionally, the study introduced three evaluation metrics: Tri-Aspect Benchmark (TAB), Token-Based Cost Effectiveness Metric (TBCEM), and Fernando's Cost-Performance Index (FCPI); to assess the performance and cost-effectiveness of the corresponding LLMs, ensuring producing content is therapeutically valuable and cost-efficient. GPT -4o Mini emerged as the optimal model, balancing therapeutic value and cost-efficiency for generating AVT content.

articleTitle: The Advanced Digital Acne Type Diagnostic System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper introduces the Advanced Digital Acne Type Diagnostic Strategy, a novel approach leveraging advanced technologies for enhanced acne vulgaris diagnosis and classification. The system integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) to accurately classify five acne types-comedones, cysts, nodules, papules, and pustules-from user-uploaded images. It further incorporates instance segmentation and object detection models for comprehensive acne severity assessment, guiding tailored treatment recommendations based on severity and acne type. Moreover, the study pioneers synthetic data generation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and stable diffusion models to create a diverse dataset of acne images, addressing the scarcity and diversity limitations of existing clinical datasets. Results demonstrate the system's efficacy in improving early acne detection, facilitating timely interventions, and enhancing patient outcomes through accessible, real-time digital diagnostics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Soft Skills in Autistic Children: The Next Generation of Mind Champ's Technological Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) significantly impacts a child's ability to navigate social interactions, regulate emotions, and develop adaptive skills crucial for daily functioning. While various interventions exist to address cognitive and academic skills, the development of soft skills such as communication, emotional regulation, social interaction, and creativity remains an under explored area. This paper builds upon the foundational work of the Mind Champ platform, which originally targeted both learning and soft skills, by focusing exclusively on enhancing the soft skills development of autistic children. This enhanced version of the Mind Champ platform leverages advanced behavioral and emotional analysis techniques to offer a comprehensive technological solution. Through interactive activities centered on painting and music, the platform creates a structured, engaging, and supportive environment tailored to the unique needs of children with ASD. By prioritizing emotional engagement and creative expression, the platform empowers children to improve their social abilities, emotional regulation, and adaptability. The results from our continued research indicate that these technology-driven interventions contribute significantly to the holistic development of soft skills in autistic children, providing them with valuable tools to navigate social environments more effectively.

articleTitle: Improving Fake News Detection with a Mixture of Experts: Leveraging Sentiment Analysis and Sarcasm Detection as Core Expert Models
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Fake news continues to proliferate, posing an increasing threat to public discourse. The paper proposes a framework of a Mixture of Experts, Sentiment Analysis, and Sarcasm Detection experts for improved fake news detection. This approach captures the emotional cues in the text through a Sentiment Analysis expert, which is based on bidirectional encoder representations from Transformers (BERT) models with sentiment vectors generated using SentiWordNet and Integrated Gradients. It combines a sarcasm detection expert based on BERT, recognizing sarcasm and its type to help classify fake news. By fusing these experts through a Mixture of Experts gateway, subtle linguistic cues often found in fake news are more effectively analyzed, leading to improved accuracy in detecting misinformation. Experimental results are presented as 96% for the Sarcasm expert with the BERT base model and 83% for the Sentiment Analysis expert with the distilled version of the BERT (DistilBERT) base model, proving the effectiveness of the proposed approach in beating traditional methods.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Using 1-of-m and Log-m Character-Level Embedding Algorithms with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Nowadays, most people around the world use social media platforms to express their feelings, ideas, opinions or other sentiments with each other by using their own native languages. To identify of those sentiments, the feature extraction process needs to be performed with help of human experts in the sentiment classification. It is very difficult to perform feature extraction approach without the help of human experts for non-English languages such as Sinhala, Tamil, or any other languages. The purpose of this research is to perform POSITIVE and NEGATIVE sentiment classification of sentences in Sinhala, which is one of the non-English language, using CNN models with the application of character level embedding algorithms named 1-of-m and Log-m. These character-level embedding algorithms construct binary image representation of the sentences before classification. This research uses 9048 Sinhala news comments labeled as POSITIVE (2490), NEGATIVE (2520), and NEUTRAL (4038). However, POSITIVE and NEGATIVE comments were selected due to 0.92 of Cohen's Kappa value. The datasets were split as 80% of training and 20% of testing data. Cross-validation showed that 1-of-m outperformed Log-m with the average testing accuracy of 66.00% and loss value of 0.6461, with precision, recall, F1 scores of 66.22%, 65.41%, and 65.79% respectively.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Detection System for Identifying Deepfake Images and Social Bots
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper presents a machine learning-based approach to detect two major forms of misinformation on social media platforms: deepfake images and social bots. For deepfake image detection, we propose a novel hybrid model combining DenseNet121 with custom Convolutional Neural Networks, achieving 97% accuracy on a dataset of 140,000 images. The social bot detection component utilizes a dual-branch architecture, processing tweet content through LSTM networks and user metadata through dense layers, attaining 91 % accuracy on the CIC truth seeker dataset. Both models demonstrate balanced performance across classes, addressing the challenges of evolving misinformation tactics. By integrating these detection systems, we aim to enhance the integrity and reliability of information ecosystems in digital spaces. Our approach contributes to the ongoing efforts to combat the spread of misinformation on social media platforms.

articleTitle: Facial Diagnosis Skin Care and Makeup Recommendation Using Advanced Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This research presents specifically an enhanced model of skin condition identification, skin color analysis, and makeup suggestion based on machine learning. The system combines a Custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), XGBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) to help in determining skin conditions including; acne, pimples, and dark spots. The Custom CNN proves to yield higher accuracy in comparison with other models such as VGG and ResNet. Further, the skin tone, which is an important characteristic of a face mask, is formulated by paying much attention to individual facial areas or specifically the cheeks to determine the most popular color that is then compared to certain categories of skin tone. Recommendations for makeup are made using both content based and collaborative filtering approach depending on the color of the skin preference of the user. According to the results of the experimental studies, the proposed model based on the Custom CNN, XGBoost, and SVM has the high accuracy of predictions; at the same time, the use of the hybrid recommendation system allows improving the individualization of makeup recommendations. The benefit of this approach is that there is a general enhancement in the field of personalised skincare and beauty solutions.

articleTitle: Exploring Radiologists' Reluctance Towards Machine Learning Models and Explainable AI in Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models have made significant advancements in medical sciences, yet their application in clinical practice is hindered by concerns over transparency and accountability. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) emerges as a solution to these challenges, offering interpretable insights into ML model predictions for clinicians. This research investigates the extent to which existing XAI techniques support decision-making in brain tumor detection for radiologists. A highly accurate ML model based on the VGG16 architecture was developed for detecting brain tumors from MRI images, achieving training and testing accuracy of 99.46% and 96.28%, respectively. A series of experiments were conducted integrating various XAI techniques. The study reveals, despite high model accuracy, false positives can mislead clinical decisions, especially when datasets contain multiple MRI sequences with conflicting diagnostic information. The findings, validated by expert radiologists, underscore the importance of using 3D imaging or at least consecutive 2D slices from the same sequence to improve diagnostic accuracy. The paper presents the experimental details highlighting the critical gap between 2D MRI slice-based diagnosis and the need for comprehensive 3D analysis. The research concludes with recommendations for improved dataset design and the integration of XAI to enhance the reliability and accountability of AI -driven healthcare diagnostic systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Mobile Application for Personalized Hair Care Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Recent advancements in computer vision and machine learning have enabled personalized hair care, advancing beyond traditional methods by catering to individual hair types and health. This paper presents Glowllp, a mobile application that provides personalized hair care recommendations through three primary modules: image quality assessment, hair type detection, and health prediction. The image quality assessment module employs edge detection and SVM classifiers to filter blurry images, achieving over 95% accuracy. For hair type classification, a hybrid model of Mask R-CNN and Vision Transformers (ViTs) identifies hair types with 92% accuracy. The health assessment module predicts hair loss and other conditions using Random Forest and XGBoost models with an F1 score of 0.91, while K-means clustering further tailor's recommendations. By integrating these modules, Glow Up delivers a comprehensive, user-friendly solution that enhances hair care personalization.

articleTitle: Smart Walking Cane for Enhanced Mobility and Safety of Visually Impaired Residents
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This paper outlines designing and constructing an intelligent walking cane to assist visually impaired individuals. The smart walking cane employed in this paper provides advanced functionality such as object recognition, path planning, obstacle avoidance through Radar, Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) detection, and navigation through the path to the desired object using wheels attached to the base of the walking cane. An overhead camera detects ArUco Markers on objects and obstacles, generating a path using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{A}^*$</tex> algorithm sent to the cane's motor wheels to guide the user. An RFID scanner reads object details, relayed through a Bluetooth earpiece, and a buzzer alerts the user of obstacles for safe navigation. The experimental results demonstrate accurate object recognition and path navigation so the user can locate the target object successfully. The proposed smart cane system shows an overall of 86.65 % by comparing the navigation path of a non-disabled person with a visually impaired person.

articleTitle: Development of a Predictive IoT-Based System for Real-Time Air Quality Monitoring and Route Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: Sri Lanka faces significant air pollution challenges, primarily from vehicular emissions, posing serious public health risks and impacting the quality of life. To address this, we developed a real-time air quality monitoring system that visualizes pollution data through an interactive heatmap. Our system integrates gas sensors that measure methane (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), sulfur dioxide (SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), and particulate matter (PM.), connected to an ESP32 board and Wi-Fi module, and strategically deployed around smart buildings. The collected data is transmitted to a central hub using IoT technology and visualized on a mobile app developed with Flutter, featuring a color-coded scheme to represent pollution levels. This allows users to easily identify high-risk areas and select cleaner routes for travel.
